10.1002_adfm.79058: γ‐ray irradiation facilitates controllable, clean, and reagent‐free cross‐linking of polymer networks without side reactions. Leveraging these merits, we precisely tune the irradiation dose to engineer a three‐dimensional (3D) poly(vinyl alcohol) (PVA) binder network for lithium‐sulfur (Li─S) batteries. By integrating multiscale synchrotron radiation X‐ray characterization techniques, we elucidate how the γ‐ray irradiation dose governs the 3D network structure and consequently regulates sulfur cathode stability and sulfur reaction kinetics without using catalysts. The optimal dose of 3 kGy yields a favorable PVA binder network featuring a dense framework, favorable connectivity, and homogeneous spatial distribution. The interpenetrating structure composed of binder, sulfur, and conductive agent leads to coupling of the mechanical architecture with the electron‐conductive network, accompanied by high‐flux lithium‐ion diffusion, thereby relieving cathode volume variation and promoting sulfur interconversion kinetics. This resulting sulfur cathode delivers a capacity decay rate of only 0.045% per cycle over 1000 cycles at 1 C. Moreover, a 1.23 Ah‐level pouch cell fabricated with the 3 kGy dose‐enabled PVA (3‐PVA) binder achieves an energy density of 390.2 Wh kg −1 . This study highlights γ‐ray irradiation as a clean and controllable strategy to engineer binder topological structure, disclosing dose‐dependent structure–property relationships that govern electrode mechanics and electrochemistry.
10.1002_adfm.79142: Carbazole‐based self‐assembled monolayers (SAMs), exemplified by [4‐(3,6‐dimethyl‐9H‐carbazol‐9‐yl)butyl]phosphonic acid (Me‐4PACz), are widely used as hole‐selective contacts in efficient perovskite/silicon tandem solar cells (TSCs). However, aggregation‐driven intermolecular organization in solution adversely affects the homogenization of SAMs on the substrate, compromising the performance of tandem devices. Herein, a supramolecular co‐assembly strategy is developed to modulate solution‐state intermolecular organization and suppress aggregation by introducing 4‐fluorophenylglycine hydrochloride, which co‐assembles with Me‐4PACz via dual‐site non‐covalent interactions. This strategy links solution‐state modulation to the formation of uniform SAM films, simultaneously realizing optimized energy alignment and reducing residual stress at the buried interface. Champion power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 23.66% and 33.91% (certified 33.5%) are achieved for 1.67 eV wide‐bandgap perovskite solar cells and 1 cm 2 two‐terminal monolithic perovskite/silicon TSCs, respectively. Moreover, the optimized tandem devices exhibit excellent operational stability under the ISOS‐L‐2 protocol, retaining 91% of the initial PCE after 1000 h of maximum power point tracking under one‐sun continuous illumination.
10.1021_jacs.6c06376: The heterogeneous interface region serves as a critical domain in lithium metal batteries, where electrons, ions, and chemical reactions interact, significantly affecting cycling reversibility. However, the ion transport mechanism of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) still lacks quantitative characterization. Using Li metal mixed inorganic compounds as a model system, we correlate and quantify the Li + exchange rates of key SEI inorganic components by applying the saturation-recovery method and establishing a two-site chemical exchange model. We not only quantitatively reveal the interfacial ion exchange rate between lithium metal and its SEI via a selective nuclear magnetic resonance exchange spectroscopy (EXSY NMR) technique but also demonstrate a close connection between interfacial transport and lithium deposition morphology by a COMSOL simulation. Furthermore, through multiscale characterization including cross-polarization (CP) NMR and cryoelectron microscopy (cryo-EM), we elucidate the Li + transport mechanisms within the actual SEI: Li 2 O can facilitate rapid Li + transport, whereas the Li + transport of LiF is highly dependent on building an interface with Li 2 O. On the basis of these new kinetic insights, we construct a Li 2 S artificial SEI using atomic layer deposition (ALD), successfully achieving 99.5% Coulombic efficiency and promoting uniform and dense lithium deposition. Our findings provide valuable design principles for engineering efficient SEIs in future lithium metal batteries.
